# Decisions: drive-visibility

Ruling 1.1(d) on task titles through APNs moves to sofar-cloud. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17.** over Specifying the APNs sender, Live Activity lifecycle and alert rules inside drive-visibility 4.3, and asking the engine record to rule whether task titles may transit APNs. because The operator: push notifications are part of the Mac app, which ships as a paid product from the separate sofar-cloud repo. Keeping the engine to data and signals means the MIT engine carries no paid-app surface, and the APNs content question is decided where the sender is built.
- 2026-09-17T15:09:57.567Z — rule: **Take the run lock with flock semantics only — never fcntl/lockf, SQLite locks, sockets or pid files — so Node, Rust and Swift contend on the same lock.** — chose **1.1(a): the run lock is an flock-semantics exclusive lock on a file keyed by run id. Rust takes it with std File::try_lock (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows; no new crate under rust-core D1), Swift with flock, Node on macOS with fs.openSync(O_EXLOCK|O_NONBLOCK) (verified 2026-09-17 on Node 24.15 to contend with flock, held through SIGSTOP, released on kill -9). Node on Linux holds it through a flock(1) child tied to the driver until sofar-core binaries ship and take over; where flock(1) is absent the driver keeps today's refusal and says liveness cannot be checked. Windows follows sofar-core. Engines floor stays >=18. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over A listening unix socket (blocked by Claude Code's Linux seccomp and macOS Seatbelt sandboxes, stale socket files after kill -9, 104-byte path limit); node:sqlite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE (needs Node >=22.13 and a rusqlite crate on the Rust side, and SQLite's fcntl locks do not see flock on Linux); pid or hostname-pid files; heartbeat locks (proper-lockfile). because rust-core D1 moves status, statusline and hook handlers to Rust while `sofar drive` stays TypeScript, and the Mac app reads through the Rust core, so the lock's readers will be Rust and Swift. flock is the primitive both get with zero new dependencies, and Node can already take the same lock on macOS; the research is in note 01M2QX4KSFFX2QV68YG4QFSKA4.
- 2026-09-17T15:10:01.087Z — rule: **Never write a pid or any content into a run lock file, never place it under the repo, and never unlink it.** — chose **1.1(b): QUALIFIES in-session-drive D2 (no pid in the record, no pid file beside it) without overturning it. An empty lock file under the per-user state dir ($XDG_STATE_HOME/sofar or ~/.local/state/sofar), whose liveness answer comes only from whether the OS reports the lock held, is not the pid file D2 forbids. D2's rule stands for pids. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over Reading D2 as forbidding any driver-owned file (leaving no way to tell a live driver from a dead one), or writing a pid into the lock file for diagnostics. because D2's reasons were that a pid is machine-local in a committed log and a reused pid signals a stranger. An empty file outside the repo carries nothing to commit and nothing to reuse: the kernel releases the lock when the holder dies, so no stale value can ever point at another process.
- 2026-09-17T15:10:06.162Z — rule: **Send driver presence only for cloud-linked repos, carrying ids only (run, initiative, task, state, seq, interval) — never content, never a record event, never analytics.** — chose **1.1(c): the driver's presence ping is user-facing sync, not telemetry emission — the CLAUDE.md guard-rail "DO NOT build … telemetry emission" is NAMED here and does not apply to it. Conditions that keep it sync: sent only for repos the operator linked to their own sofar cloud account, with an opt-out; payload is ids only; shown only to that repo's members; one server row per run, overwritten, deleted after the run; never used for product analytics; never written to events.jsonl. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over Treating the ping as telemetry and dropping remote presence (remote viewers could never tell a crashed driver from a running one), or folding presence into the record as periodic events. because Telemetry is data about the product's use sent to its maker; this ping is the operator's own run state delivered to the operator's own devices through sync they opted into, the same class as `sofar push`. The conditions make that distinction checkable rather than asserted.
- 2026-09-17T15:10:10.660Z — rule: **Never block a detached or agent-launched run on a keep-awake prompt; prompt only on a TTY, otherwise state the unset setting in the preflight lines.** — chose **1.1(e): keep-awake lives in the engine. On macOS the driver spawns `caffeinate -i -w <its own pid>` for the run's life. Setting `drive.keep_awake` (on/off) in ~/.config/sofar/config.json; a terminal run with the setting unset asks once and saves the answer; a detached or agent-launched run never prompts, and its preflight lines say the setting is unset so the agent asks the operator in chat; `--keep-awake` / `--no-keep-awake` override per run; the opening lines state that idle sleep is blocked but lid-close sleep is not. The paid Mac app may toggle the same setting. Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over Keep-awake only in the paid Mac app (works only while the app runs, and cannot tie itself to the driver's lifetime); always on (surprising power use); a per-repo setting committed to git (sleep is a machine preference, not project state). because Only the driver knows its own lifetime, and `caffeinate -w` ends by itself when the watched process exits, so no cleanup and no pid is stored anywhere. The operator asked for a way to be asked before a run and a setting to turn it on or off.
- 2026-09-17T15:10:14.171Z — rule: **Never add licence, plan or entitlement checks to the engine; paid features are enforced by sofar-cloud's server.** — chose **1.1(f): sync during a run (4.1) and driver presence (4.2) are paid features, following sofar-cloud v2-sync-team D2 ("sync IS the paid product"). sofar-cloud enforces entitlement on its push and presence endpoints; the MIT engine carries only the client code, acts only for linked repos, and on an entitlement refusal says so once and keeps the run going unsynced. Local pieces — run lock, fencing, --await, --follow, prompt line, statusline, keep-awake — touch no cloud and stay free. Paid pieces are designed for a 100-person repo first (sofar-cloud enterprise D1). Ruled by the operator 2026-09-17 ("yes to all").** over Shipping drive-time sync free in the engine, or gating it with licence code inside the engine. because The engine is MIT (packages/engine/package.json), so a paywall in its code can be deleted by anyone; the server is the only place entitlement holds. Keeping the protection pieces free avoids charging users to prevent damage to their own repos.
